groups.name: Scientific data sources
groups.description: Archive and publication records by role. Global relief and imagery are separate from regional stereo elevation. Jezero assets remain an example, with coverage and exact product selection evaluated per region.

groups.name: Discovery & registry
groups.description: Discover and normalize asset metadata, index footprints, and select versioned input assets by objective. An indexed footprint is evidence of possible coverage; it does not establish valid-pixel support.

groups.name: Acquisition & ingestion
groups.description: Acquire full, tiled, local or windowed inputs with verified capabilities. Preserve unaltered source bytes and labels separately from derivatives. Quarantine unreadable or corrupt assets.

groups.name: Mars spatial reference
groups.description: Shared Mars coordinate conventions and transform verification for planetary indexing, polar coverage and per-region metric analysis. Carry native and destination horizontal and vertical references.

groups.name: Global Mars atlas
groups.description: Precompute a multi-resolution visual atlas, contextual elevation and scientific overlays. Record actual footprint and resolution by layer. Offline scope is a selected atlas subset and selected region packs.

groups.name: Region evaluation
groups.description: Accept an arbitrary set of candidate region records, including the current 56-region research effort. Keep scientific judgment, availability and suitability separate. Prioritization can authorize investigation; readiness requires independent gates.

groups.name: Regional processing
groups.description: Turn a selected region and pinned assets into local terrain crops and independently processed optical and geology overlays. Jezero is a reference case; regions can vary in data, projection and output capabilities.

groups.name: Terrain & routing inputs
groups.description: Prepare baseline analytical elevation, native gradient, validity and screening arrays. Supply inputs to the directed runtime solver. Explicitly withhold detailed routing on insufficient terrain.

groups.name: Science & evidence
groups.description: Preserve observations, interpreted features, candidate targets and hypothetical approach stations as distinct, linked records. Orbital and published science can support a region without rover observations.

groups.name: Integration & quality
groups.description: Integrate independently processed layers, record gate outcomes and classify capability. Every gate starts Not evaluated. Required failures block the affected capability; optional failures may yield a documented partial release.

groups.name: Packaging & publication
groups.description: Publish validated, versioned atlas assets and regional packs to a local registry. Deliver a bounded offline subset. Exact storage location, tile encoding and distribution policy are engineering decisions.

groups.name: Build provenance
groups.description: One shared build configuration and lineage ledger ties source versions, methods, transforms, software, reports and artifacts together. Versions are reproducible and releases immutable.

groups.name: Crew interface
groups.description: A tablet-friendly planning and field workspace for a fictional two-person crew. Compare baseline and updated decisions with a time ledger, retained and deferred science and source evidence.

groups.name: Planning API
groups.description: The local Python service serves the cell-first Explore workflow, regional evidence, ranking and simulated planning. The HEALPix ID is canonical. Named Atlas features are approximate anchors. Reviewed evidence is bound by package and query digests.

groups.name: Mission optimization
groups.description: Compose candidate plans, account for resources, filter hard constraints, then compare feasible alternatives and select by declared mission priorities.

groups.name: Terrain routing
groups.description: Build directed, weighted adjacency from the prepared grid. Apply closure exclusions per request. Solve outward travel and return-to-shelter on the appropriate graph orientations.

groups.name: Deployment
groups.description: Use the identical app and pinned data in one local process or an optional team-approved container host. Keep a labeled offline replay for live-demo failure.

groups.name: Validation
groups.description: Planned acceptance checks and measurements. Catalog presence does not validate the pack, routes, decisions or real EVA performance.

groups.name: Mission configuration
groups.description: Versioned mission state, tagged human/rover profiles, authorized constraints and distinct scenario/evidence inputs.

groups.name: Planetary geometry
groups.description: Canonical pack geometry and local directed edge quantities. Geographic distance is for discovery; only valid local analytical geometry feeds detailed paths.

groups.name: Traversability
groups.description: Coverage, resolution, supported derived roughness and mapped exclusions. Qualitative surface interpretation never supplies an uncalibrated cost.

groups.name: Human Marswalk
groups.description: Transparent illustrative walking time and authorized constraints, without physiological or individual health predictions.

groups.name: Rover mobility
groups.description: Vehicle-specific feasibility, effective speed and electrical accounting. Quantitative wheel-ground mechanics require relevant data and validation.

groups.name: Environmental models
groups.description: Historical and simulated inputs are marked. Each environmental model needs purpose, valid domain and input evidence before affecting constraints.

groups.name: Resource budgets
groups.description: Separate time, energy and authorized consumables with return reserves and prefix checks where required.

groups.name: Science value & tasks
groups.description: Shared regional screening and evidence contracts, mission-specific priorities, prerequisites and distinct feature/approach/remote observation locations.

groups.name: Dynamic replanning
groups.description: Validate updates, invalidate stale options and re-evaluate paths, budgets and science from the current state.

groups.name: Uncertainty & sensitivity
groups.description: Separate evidence gaps, model and scenario uncertainty. Scenario bounds and reason codes can limit or withhold recommendations.

groups.name: Decision explanation
groups.description: Show current feasible options, rejected alternatives, evidence, resource margins and changes from the previous plan.

decisionSteps.caption: Confirm the crew checkpoint and submit the simulated corridor closure.
Mark the previous plan as history and submit a new request with the full crew state.
Validate the event through the API, then exclude the affected cells and edges from the request graph.
Find outward paths from the checkpoint and return-to-shelter paths on the transposed graph.
Compare both route legs and time on site for each unfinished task.
Recalculate signed margins and check direct return. In the report’s illustrative 60-minute allowance with a 15-minute reserve, the transect drops from +5 to −3 minutes.
Apply the science-priority rule or abstain. Attach the sources, reason codes and expected science artifacts.
Accept only the current response. In the report’s illustrative example, oriented photos preserve bedding context at +20 minutes and defer the measured transect. Direct return keeps +33 minutes.
